sections.html:
Oskaloosa, with 11,558 residents, is the seat of Mahaska County and dwarfs every other town in it. The whole county held 22,190 people in 2020. After it come New Sharon (1,262), Eddyville (970) and Fremont (708), plus small communities such as Beacon and University Park. The population has hardly changed since 1980, so ownership here is stable and houses tend to change hands slowly.

Hot summers and cold winters wear on older houses, so roofs, furnaces and gutters are where an inspector begins. Think about that when you weigh repairs against selling as-is. Coal mining once shaped the county, and some rural parcels carry long paper trails. The courthouse holds the deeds and parcel records.

Find both offices in the Mahaska County Courthouse at 106 South 1st Street, Oskaloosa. Value is the Assessor's job, and collection belongs to the Treasurer.

OfficePhoneHours
Assessor(641) 673-58058:00 am to 4:30 pm, Monday to Friday
Treasurer (property tax)(641) 673-54828:00 am to 4:30 pm, Monday to Friday

Online, the Assessor page offers Beacon maps and records, a report of recent sales, and a Data Correction Form reachable from any parcel report. Built an addition or lost an outbuilding? Email the office your address and a phone number.

Pull up your parcel in Beacon before anything else. From April 2 to April 25 the Assessor will take an informal review request, and the written protest deadline is April 30. The dates are statewide rules found in Iowa Code 441.37 and Department of Revenue guidance.

Use the state form for a written protest, signed by you or your agent. A board may allow electronic filing. Owners can also correct clerical or mathematical errors going back to earlier years, if those years are not fully paid.

  • Aim at the January 1 value, since that is the date assessments reflect.
  • Arguing the value is too high? Bring recent sales close to your house.
  • Claiming the wrong class? Bring proof of how the house is actually used.

Protest hearings before the local board of review begin May 1, and the board should finish by May 31. The state may allow more time, though never beyond July 15. Its written decision has to be mailed within three days of adjourning.

If you remain unconvinced, the Property Assessment Appeal Board and district court are the next steps. You have 20 days counted from adjournment or May 31, whichever falls later. Board members serve six-year staggered terms, and at least one must be a farmer (see the Iowa Department of Revenue summary).

Iowa Code chapter 445 makes the first half delinquent October 1 and the second half April 1. A half that is late accrues one and one-half percent interest per month or partial month.

The interest figure is rounded to a whole dollar, and it is never less than $1. Options for paying are the Iowa Treasurers' parcel search online, the courthouse counter, or a mailed check to 106 S 1st Street. Ahead of a closing, phone (641) 673-5482 for exact amounts on your parcel.

Every June, usually the third Monday, treasurers across Iowa put delinquent parcels up for sale. The buyer covers the taxes, interest, fees and costs. Redemption by the owner afterward takes the sale price, a certificate fee and 2% interest per month (Iowa Code 446.7 and 447.1).

Inherited a house that carries back taxes? Ask the Treasurer about the parcel right away. It is far better to learn the balance now than from a notice after the auction.

sections.h2: Taxes and filings when you sell
sections.html:
The transfer tax works out to 80 cents per $500 of value beyond the first $500. When the deed is filed, a declaration of value accompanies it; the recorder forwards that to the assessor, who retains it three years (Iowa Code 428A.1).

Homestead credit timing can matter to your closing date. When a house sells before July 1, the buyer must claim the credit by July 1. When it sells on or after July 1, the credit remains with the property that year (rule 701-110.1).

  • Tax is a lien on the parcel that ranks ahead of everyone but the state.
  • Tax paid in error can be refunded only if you claim it within two years of the due date.
  • A treasurer's receipt showing full payment is conclusive proof that the parcel was free of taxes.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes owed, step by step
sections.html:
First, phone the Treasurer at (641) 673-5482 for the balance on your parcel, interest included. Second, read your Beacon parcel report for mistakes in size, class or buildings. If you find one, send the Data Correction Form, and think about a protest when April comes.

Third, choose how to sell. Listing the traditional way means getting the house ready, waiting on a financed buyer and often answering repair requests. Selling as-is for cash skips most of it. Either way, unpaid tax is deducted from the price when you close, the buyer receives the parcel free of it, and the treasurer's receipt documents that. Have the closing agent confirm the payoff figure shortly beforehand, since another month of interest can change it.

Pull together three items: a payoff statement, the parcel record and a list of repairs or damage. Together they show how your balance compares with what the house might bring.

  • Pull the Beacon parcel report and use the Data Correction Form for wrong details.
  • Get today's amount from the Treasurer, interest included.
  • For an inherited house, confirm at the courthouse who the owners of record are.
  • See whether the Assessor has a homestead credit on file, and let the buyer know.

Suppose the balance is bigger than you expected or the repair list is long. A cash buyer taking the house as-is can settle the taxes at closing and relieve you of the repairs. Set that offer beside what a listing would net before deciding. Neither choice should be made in a hurry, and the June sale is the date to keep in view.

faqs.q: Where is the Mahaska County Assessor's office?
faqs.a: Look on the first floor of the Mahaska County Courthouse, in the southeast corner, at 106 South 1st Street, Oskaloosa, IA 52577. The phone is (641) 673-5805, and staff are in weekdays 8:00 am to 4:30 pm.

faqs.q: What is the property tax protest window in Mahaska County?
faqs.a: It opens April 2 and closes April 30 under state law. For an informal review with the Assessor, use April 2 through April 25.

faqs.q: How can I pay Mahaska County property tax?
faqs.a: Use the Iowa Treasurers' parcel search online, come to the courthouse on a weekday, or mail payment to 106 S 1st Street. Questions go to (641) 673-5482.

faqs.q: How much is the late fee on Iowa property tax?
faqs.a: Late interest is one and one-half percent monthly. It rounds to the dollar, never below $1, and part of a month is billed as a whole month.

faqs.q: Is Oskaloosa the biggest city in Mahaska County?
faqs.a: Yes, with 11,558 residents in 2020. It is also the county seat.
